unit_label: BRBL Module B unit 5: Securities and modes of charge I — Separate mortgage formalities, document operating time and general priority from assumptions based only on registration date

facts.statement: Courseware gives section 59 formality, general earlier-right priority, registration operating-time discussion and the title-deed-mortgage exception; blanket cost/registration claims are held back.
facts.locator: S04 printed pp. 189, 191–192; PDF page = printed page + 19

facts.statement: Section 59 describes registered, signed and two-witness-attested formality for the specified principal amount and non-title-deed-deposit mortgages, with stated smaller-amount rules. Section 48 sets the general earlier-created-right priority subject to its special-contract/reservation qualification. These provisions do not certify every state stamp requirement or every memorandum of deposit.
facts.locator: sections 48 and 59, official Delhi text headings
sections 47–50, PDF pp. 1–2; section 47 page visually inspected
facts.statement: Section 47 gives the operating-time rule; section 48 includes a proviso for a title-deed mortgage against a later executed/registered mortgage-deed. Section 49 gives qualified consequences and evidential exceptions; section 50 also has qualifications. State-amendment commentary must be scoped separately.

payload.title: Read the formality rule together with its limits
payload.core_explanation_md:
Section 59 sets a central-text rule for mortgages securing principal of Rs 100 or more, other than a mortgage by deposit of title deeds: the specified registered instrument, mortgagor signature and at least two attesting witnesses are required. Its smaller-amount rules also have qualifications.

The exception for title-deed deposit must not become “every paper recording that deposit is always exempt from registration and stamp duty”. The function of a memorandum, applicable state amendments, stamp law and separate filing obligations need their own sources. Classification under section 58(f) and the formalities of a particular instrument are connected questions, but they are not interchangeable.

self_check.prompt_text: Does the section 59 exception by itself establish that every deposit memorandum is free of all registration and stamp requirements?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The instrument's function and applicable legal requirements need separate review.

payload.title: Do not decide competing rights from the registry timestamps alone
payload.core_explanation_md:
Section 48 of the Transfer of Property Act gives a general earlier-created-right rule where competing rights cannot all operate fully together, subject to the stated special-contract or reservation qualification. Section 47 of the Registration Act concerns when a registered document operates: it does not simply choose the day registration occurred.

For a hypothetical pair of valid instruments stipulated to operate from execution, a later registration timestamp alone does not prove later priority. Record creation, operative effect, registration, validity and any binding priority arrangement. The title-deed-mortgage proviso in Registration Act section 48 is another reason not to apply an unqualified “registered always defeats unregistered” shortcut.

self_check.prompt_text: Which dates and terms belong in a competing-security file besides registration dates?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Creation and operative dates, validity and any binding priority arrangement or statutory qualification.

payload.stem_md: Two valid mortgage instruments are stipulated to operate from execution, with no special priority agreement or other exception. A was executed on 10 June and registered on 20 June; B was executed on 14 June and registered on 18 June. What should be corrected in a note awarding B priority solely for earlier registration?

options.text_md: The two instruments necessarily have equal priority because both are registered
options.explanation_md: Registration of both does not erase the difference in when their competing rights were created and operate.

options.text_md: Whichever lender first demands payment must always rank first
options.explanation_md: Demand timing is not the stipulated basis of the general earlier-right and operating-time analysis.

options.text_md: Registration timestamps alone do not defeat A's earlier operative creation on these stated assumptions
options.explanation_md: The general priority and operating-time rules require the stipulated creation/effect facts, not registry completion order alone.

options.text_md: A cannot have any legal effect because its registration followed its execution
options.explanation_md: Registration after execution is not itself the defect asserted here; both instruments are stipulated valid.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The general priority and operating-time rules require the stipulated creation/effect facts, not registry completion order alone.

payload.stem_md: A bank policy says a title-deed deposit means every related memorandum is automatically exempt from every registration and stamp requirement. Which review response is justified by the evidence?

options.text_md: Check the instrument's operative function and applicable state/formality law rather than extend the section 59 exception universally
options.explanation_md: A mortgage-category exception does not by itself answer every document, state amendment and stamp-law question.

options.text_md: Treat the policy as a substitute for the statutory formality analysis
options.explanation_md: An internal policy cannot replace the governing legal requirements.

options.text_md: Assume a notarised copy cures every registration defect
options.explanation_md: Notarisation cannot be assumed to satisfy a separate registration requirement.

options.text_md: Conclude that title-deed mortgages can never be created at all
options.explanation_md: The statute expressly recognises that mortgage form; rejecting it universally is the opposite unsupported blanket rule.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A mortgage-category exception does not by itself answer every document, state amendment and stamp-law question.
